rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep banned_words body_hits 0 CLEAN; em_dash 0 CLEAN; leverage_verb 0 CLEAN (planted_proof true on each). Harm (flinch words, silent em-dash rewrite) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep ritual_ceremony body_hits 0 CLEAN; 'practice' as noun: grep -cE '\bpractice\b' over lines 1-121 -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps session_biography 0 and dated_line 0 CLEAN in body. Closest transition-shaped line is L102 'Claude has been painting this box for half an hour', a present-state fact about the session, not a record of an edit. Maintainer L124-154 read for transition verbs: each clause states current wiring (Role, Reuse, Board, Artefacts); the only date is the Quality stamp line the stamper writes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L46 'It is also a box your nearest competitor could print with their logo on it.' concrete Sutherland-style reframe in peer warmth; no atmospheric or body-state imagery found; no retain-this wrapper (grep 'Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget' -> 0); no negation-callout contradicted by its paragraph.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L52 credits the move by originator inline ('Amazon teams write the press release ... call it working backwards'); the practitioner chain (Bryar and Carr, Hohmann) sits in maintainer L133, which the rule allows. grep 'Antti|the creator|the author|course creator' over body -> 0; grep '\b[Ww]e\b' over body -> 0 (no author-we).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view the_student 0 CLEAN. Closest L19 'The trainer posts both in chat' names the facilitator only for where the board and team folder come from, the sparing use the rule allows.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest coinages L76 'only-us' and L88 'never-say' are defined at point of use (L70 'things your product does that a competitor's doesn't'; L82 'the words they would never use about your product'). 'driver' is defined L17. No maintainer-only term (frameworks list L133) appears in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Over-hedge flags (no penalty, fine way to, it's OK if, not on the hook) -> none in body. Closest L34 'if your company hasn't turned it on, paste a screenshot instead' is a plausible-failure fallback, not an absolution. L56 'Claude knows working backwards already. The tune here:' states the division of labour and stops.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only attribution in student prose is L52 'Amazon teams' (a company, once); no practitioner name repeated.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest punchy line L108 'You told Claude different things between the two, and nothing else changed.' holds inside this exercise's own scope (same model, same file, five changed inputs), so no overreach needing a downstream carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c vendor over body -> 0; flag phrases (not an aspirational, this isn't marketing, grounded in actual, from the person running it) -> 0. Closest L70 'Every product in your category promises speed, ease and peace of mind.' is the baseline-generic setup, not positioning defence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest operational copy: L34 'Miro connector' (glossed by function in the same sentence: Claude reads the board through it, with a screenshot fallback) and the prompts' 'subagent' (fence 6; the why sits in L102). 'working backwards' is defined at first use L52 before any prompt echoes it. No LLM-internal vocabulary (token, embedding, schema) in lead-ins or headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closer L120 'Keep the generic line the fresh read found; it is the first thing to fix.' 'it' resolves to one noun (the generic line) and the action is concrete (keep, then fix). L62 'the sticky's author moves it' reads two ways (see notes) but is mid-paragraph, not a closer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `
rules_evaluated.evidence: **What happened:** at L114 is optional and earns its slot: the exercise leaves a durable artifact (team/product-box.html) the next exercises consume. Past tense ('The first came from your public page'). Grep tell '^\*\*What happened:\*\* You' -> 0 (content starts 'Same model, five boxes', count + noun). Longer than the 25-40 word shape (about 44 words, four sentences) but not a replay of the phases; the destination move lives in the adjacent **What's next:** block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Combative-verb scan of body: bark/order/command/whip/force/drag/boss/scold about the agent -> none. Closest L94 'Steal a look by naming it' is about borrowing a design reference, and L110 'Push back' is the corpus's peer-flat idiom for steering.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers read true against their sections: L48 'Write it backwards from your customer' matches the working-backwards pass; L98 'A fresh read' matches the cold subagent read (L98-L110); L112 'Take stock of the box' matches the recap. No 'other X' or spatial metaphor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L82 'Not categories (*"complexity"*) but the real complaint' negates the reader's actual prior (maintainer failure row for Phase 4 records categories as the dominant miss). No bold-label echo, no 'That is the X' drumroll with an unresolved antecedent (L46 'It works. It reads like a box.' both resolve to 'the page' in the preceding sentence).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No count sits beside the list it counts: L15 'Five passes' and L116 'five boxes' are a handle reused away from the phase list, and phase headers carry no numeral counting items. L70 'Pick three together' is content (the count of stickies chosen), not a tally of an adjacent list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L70 'Every product in your category promises speed, ease and peace of mind.' a universal about the world, but it is the deliberately generic baseline the next lines contrast against, and a reader hears it as a type, not a claim to audit (see suggestion). L52 'the questions behind it ask for the top reasons the product could still fail' is a description of the method, not a superlative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L15 'Then a fresh read tells you which line is still generic.' the read comes from a context that did not build the box and quotes a line, so the outcome is observable (a quoted line that can be checked against the page); L64 'Ask whose sentence it is' points at a checkable source (has anyone heard a customer say it).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Style rule, not a gate. Closest L110 'Ask for the line a competitor could paste onto their own box today' echoes fence 6's 'the one a competitor could paste onto their own box today'; it is the push-back wording for a soft answer, a different job from the fence's first ask.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose stands without the trainer — no cue-card prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Muted read: every sentence carries a verb or is a verbed-sentence enumeration (L40 'Navigation, footer and all.' follows 'paste it'). Report-only grep 'on the screen|Take a guess|before it runs|Let's go|Your turn' -> 1 hit, L108 'the page on the screen', whose referent is the page painted in the preceding passage and named in the same sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L46 'It is also a box your nearest competitor could print' describes the artifact, not the student; grep 'beginner|senior|at your scale|more experienced' over body -> 0. No identity-criterion clause ('the difference is whether', 'the real test is') found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'working backwards' defined at first use L52; 'driver' L17; 'cold read' L102-L104; 'sticky' and 'frame' are product-team working vocabulary. Closest L34 'Miro connector' glossed by function in-sentence (Claude reads the board through it, screenshot fallback).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No flagged business-audience tech word in body prose L1-L121; fence-only terms are 'HTML' and 'subagent'. SVP-marketing flinch test: 'connector' is the nearest, glossed in L34.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L102 'A read with no memory of building it is sharper' uses memory for session context, loosely (see suggestion); body never claims memory or context compounds.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body stays on the golden path. Two rescues kept pass plausible-failure plus non-obvious fix: L34 'if your company hasn't turned it on, paste a screenshot' and L110 'Push back if the "most generic line" comes back soft'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts end on destination plus a report-back (team/product-box.html; 'tell me which lines you replaced or cut'). Closest shape spec: baseline fence 'The front: ... The back: who it is for' is the teaching moment (a bare generic box).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Instruction lines name actor and mechanism: L17 the designer drives, others work the board; L62 'the sticky's author moves it ... the driver asks for it back'; L64 'Ask whose sentence it is'. Look-lines carry object and tell: L46 'Open the page. It works. It reads like a box.' (object: the painted page; tell: a competitor could print it). Speech verbs ('say so' L62, 'Read the two quotes out loud' L108) address the team of three, the exercise's stated banter room. 'naming it' L94 is the one name-smell in body (see suggestion). Executable-test closest: L108 'put the Phase 1 baseline in your head' (see student_facing 18).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'What research says' callout; L52 is a two-sentence in-line definition.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Forcing function stays in chat with Claude; the non-chat moves are board work (stickies, screenshot onto the frame L96), which is the exercise's design, not a mechanic tool.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view em_dash body_hits 0 CLEAN. Closest long sentence L94 is a list sentence split by colons and periods only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 36:'## Phase 1: The boring baseline'; 66:'## Phase 3: What only your product does'; 78:'## Phase 4: What your customers would never say'; 98:'## Phase 6: A fresh read'. Four of six phase headers are noun phrases over sections where the student acts; L48 'Write it backwards...' and L90 'Make it yours' show the verb form the rule wants. Harm (headers that hide the move) is mild: each opens on a one-line action.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Lead the four noun-phrase phase headers with a command verb, or rule the Phase N: pattern a squint-test (§38) exception.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 108:'Then put the Phase 1 baseline in your head next to the page on the screen.' An ordinal used as a coordinate: reordering or inserting a phase silently repoints it, and the reader must scroll to resolve it. 'put ... in your head' also names no doable move (see suggestion).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Refer to the first box by what it is (the baseline from your public page) and name the comparison move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body Claude-count vs 'the agent' 0 is the audit-signal shape, but every use is addressee or product ('Ask Claude to ...' L23/L42/L58/L74/L86/L104, 'Claude reads the board' L34, 'Claude knows' L56). No autonomous-work sentence is phrased as Claude.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E 'tonight|tomorrow|overnight|this morning|yesterday|last night' over body -> 0. 'half an hour' L102 is a duration, not a time-of-day anchor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E 'sit with|take a moment|let it land|pause|breathe' over body -> 0; no self-aware reflection header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L62 where Claude's wording and a sticky are compared: the team decides, and no prompt asks them to restate a decision already made. Fence 2 asks about beats with no sticky, which the student has not decided.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one artifact is team/product-box.html; HTML is the native type of a page (the rule's game=.html exception).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L17 'so the latest version always lives there' tells the student which single path later agents read, which changes what they do (overwrite, not fork). L40 'The mess is the point' protects the baseline, so it moves the exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L108 'Read the two quotes out loud.' follows a chat-print but carries follow-on moves in the same paragraph (compare against the baseline) and L110 (push back), so it is not a bare 'read it'. L66 'Open the page' opens a file, not a chat-print.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closers L116-L120 take the student as subject ('Each of you can point at...', 'You keep this box', 'Keep the generic line'); no 'the training', 'watch for', or role-gating.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L7 opens the session with its working-folder path and L19 repeats 'team/' at point of use; restating is the affordance this rule keeps.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L108 'You told Claude different things between the two, and nothing else changed.' echoes the training's context-shapes-output spine (maintainer L127), earned by the five passes just run.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep 'typing|type in|say to Claude|tell it to' over body -> 0. Closest L40 'paste it after the colon' names a paste target, not a keystroke narrative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L40 'Select all, copy, and paste it after the colon.' is a three-verb recipe but 'select all' is load-bearing (maintainer failure row 1: a curated paste kills the contrast); no CLI or login walkthrough.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Subject test closest L120 'The bet is written against it next, and on Day 3 five people from outside the team look at it.' names later beats, but it sits in the **What's next:** block (the exercise's bridge signposting) and is the reason to keep team/product-box.html, which every pass otherwise overwrites. Deletion test: removing it loses the motive for 'You keep this box'. No other self-narration found in L1-L110.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood: playful first hands-on beat (L3 'Banter expected.'); setup L5-L34 is plumbing and exempt. Teaching beats L36-L110 keep the contrast open to be felt; no verification step resolves a doubt. Closer L116 leaves the felt contrast; L120 leaves the generic line as a fix to make.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers alone ('The boring baseline', 'Write it backwards from your customer', 'What only your product does', 'What your customers would never say', 'Make it yours', 'A fresh read') reconstruct a box that is made in passes and read cold; H1 'Paint the product box' names the deliverable.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-study is invisible in the training flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep 'self-study|Teacher Claude' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'session' appears at L7 only as the sitting; 'run' occurs as a verb only; grep for noun-run of the agent -> 0. 'task' is the Cowork container at L7, a product term.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded fences scanned for \[[A-Za-z][^\]]*\] -> 0 in all 6 prompt fences. Closest link fence 'team/<my-name>/' is an angle-bracket path template Claude resolves (it is told to ask for the first name); the two open-hook fences end in a colon and the body says what to paste (L40, L23).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 23:'Ask Claude to link the team folder into your training folder as `team/`, then paste the path the trainer posted.' (20 words, summarising a fence that ends 'The team folder is at:') and 42:'Ask Claude to paint a product box from your public page.' (fence ends 'Our public page:'). Both fences end in a dangling colon awaiting input, the 2a sub-case: the lead-in's whole job is naming what to drop in, and the summary in front is dead weight. Harm (a skim-cue that duplicates the fence and buries the one instruction) is present at L23.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut each lead-in to the drop-in instruction: 'Paste the path the trainer posted after the colon.' / 'Paste your page after the colon.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All six expanded fences carry '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*', a blank line, then the fence (expanded L25, L54, L80, L111, L131, L159); lead-in then marker in raw source.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chain target is the single deterministic path team/product-box.html in all five painting fences. Closest: no 'the file you just created' anchor in the repaint fences, but the path is named identically each time and L17 states every pass overwrites it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest baseline fence 'Don't ask me questions yet' hints that questions come later; it protects the generic baseline and does not defer a hard choice to a named downstream step.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No session reset offered inside a phase ('/rename' at L10 is a label, not /clear); the cold read isolates by subagent (fence 6), the rule's sanctioned route.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`
rules_evaluated.evidence: Python scan of the 6 expanded prompt fences for '*' -> False in each; no markdown shout inside fences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only the link step is runtime-forked (L21-L32: rt-code prompt vs rt-cowork paragraph); the five painting fences are runtime-agnostic. The rt-cowork fork names the concrete UI move ('+ button, next to your training folder') and keeps the canonical chip.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry — MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Cowork fork L28-L32 names the concrete UI move and the runtime consequence ('Wherever a prompt says team/, Claude uses that folder'); it is shorter than the Code fork because the Code fork's fence includes a write test, an asymmetry in verification, not in mechanics.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Append-vs-integrate — name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fences name integration: P2 'The front carries the customer's promise. The press release goes on the back, in the stickies' words'; P3 'rest on those three lines'; P4 'the voice of the whole box'. No 'add X and regenerate'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Niceness tax — name the edge or pin the line on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fences pin the edge: P3 'Every claim ... any competitor ... could also make: replace it, or cut it'; P4 'Not a list of what we're against, but the voice of the whole box'; P4 'keep the only-us lines'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Question fence states the cadence: 'ask about any beat that has no sticky, one beat at a time. Wait for my answer before the next. Don't fill a beat yourself.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every regeneration fence names destination 'team/product-box.html' with the in-place verb 'repaint', and L17 states every pass overwrites; no fence leaves overwrite-or-new open.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory everywhere per the rule; no plan-mode fence here and no run named showing preamble eating a read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fence 6 asks a reader with no part in the build, not Claude defending its work; fences 3 and 4 close with 'tell me which lines you replaced or cut' / 'quoting any never-say word you found on the old box', accounting verbs rather than defence verbs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Narrowed rule that never gates; no run named showing a downstream re-run caused by a gap at save time. The only interview fence (P2) already refuses generic answers ('Don't fill a beat yourself').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fences 3 and 4 end with a post-action report ('Then tell me which lines you replaced or cut', 'Finish by quoting any never-say word you found on the old box'); no external-trust-line action in the exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No absolute path or cd in any fence; paths are relative (team/, team/product-box.html).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Subagent appears in fence 6 only ('Spawn a subagent to read team/product-box.html cold'); the why precedes the fence at L102 ('A read with no memory of building it is sharper'), which the rule accepts when setup already makes it obvious.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every Save-it path has a named consumer: team/product-box.html is read by the next painting fence each phase, by the cold-read subagent, and per maintainer L135 by the bet exercise and Day 3.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rendered label is exactly '**Prompt**' in all six expanded fences; no custom labels.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Baseline fence is a normal work request ('Paint a product box for our product from the public page I'll paste below'); the later fences' protocol is the lesson, not front-loaded orchestration.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All six prompts are {{prompt:key}} markers on their own lines (L25, L44, L60, L76, L88, L106), each led by a sentence; no inline **Prompt** blocks in the raw body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No module numbers in any fence (grep 'M[0-9]|Module [0-9]' over expanded fences -> 0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fence in isolation runs against a realistic machine: P2 handles the unreachable board ('If you can't reach the board, say so, and I'll paste a screenshot'); P3 and P4 carry the same fallback ('or in the screenshot I paste'); the link fence tests the write itself.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2 (about 140 words) splits by move: board read, sort (bullets), show and ask, repaint, each its own paragraph; P1, P3-P6 are short and already scan by move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lead-ins rhyme with fence openings: L42 'paint a product box from your public page' / 'Paint a product box for our product from the public page'; L58 'read the box frame' / 'Read the box frame on our team's Miro board'; L74 'read the three only-us stickies' / 'Read the three only-us stickies'. Weakest: L86 'repaint the box from what your customers hate' against 'Read the hate and never-say stickies' shares noun phrases not the verb (see suggestion).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All fences run in the warm Day 1 session (L7 opens it; no /clear between phases); definite references ('the box frame', 'the old box', 'team/product-box.html') are all in scrollback or on disk by that point. Fence 6's subagent is cold by design and is handed the path.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Tail ordering: P2 ends 'Then repaint team/product-box.html', the artifact instruction is last; no trailing STOP.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P3 'Every claim on the box that any competitor in our category could also make: replace it, or cut it' is a load-bearing leading line that keeps the box off the beige default; left as is.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fences end with destination plus a report-back rather than a shape spec; closest the baseline's 'The front: ... The back: who it is for' is shape the teaching depends on (a plain box to be repainted).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: "Add X and regenerate" is a trap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'add X and regenerate' wording; the repaint fences state how the new source enters ('rest on those three lines', 'the voice of the whole box').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closing mechanic is a cold read by an independent reader (fence 6) plus saying the quotes aloud and putting the generic line on the frame; a deliberate choice for an artefact-producing exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood: leaves the student with a felt contrast between a generic box and their own (L116) and the generic line still to fix (L120), which sets up the bet exercise. Setup L5-L34 is plumbing and mood-exempt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequencing claims in body agree with the maintainer wiring: L120 'The bet is written against it next, and on Day 3 five people from outside the team look at it' matches maintainer L135 (consumed by apt101-write-the-bet and apt101-five-users). No downstream teaching moment is named or front-run in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: article rough-cut rule; file is an exercise

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
